title_content.content: UAV-Assisted Multi-Access Computation Offloading via Hybrid NOMA and FDMA in Marine Networks

paragraph_content.content: Minghui Dai , Yuan Wu , Senior Member, IEEE, Liping Qian , Senior Member, IEEE, Zhou Su , Senior Member, IEEE, Bin Lin , Senior Member, IEEE, and Nan Chen , Member, IEEE

Abstract—With the rapid development of marine networks, there have been growing demands for computation-intensive and delay-sensitive marine applications and services. However, the limited underwater energy supply and the acoustic channels result in the low efficiency for computing tasks and high transmission delay. In this paper, we investigate the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)-assisted multi-access computation offloading in marine networks, with the objective of minimizing the energy consumption of ocean devices. Specifically, for the underwater segment, we consider the scenario that multiple underwater sensor nodes (USNs) covered by the unmanned surface vehicle (USV) upload their sensing data via non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) for improving the channel utilization. For the radio frequency segment, we consider the scenario that multiple UAVs hovering in the air act as the aerial edge servers for providing computing services, in which the USV offloads the workloads to UAVs via frequency division multiple access (FDMA) for avoiding their cochannel interference, while taking into account that a malicious node overhears the USV’s offloading transmission. To improve the computation offloading efficiency, we formulate an optimization problem for USNs and USV to minimize the total energy consumption by jointly optimizing the USN’s uploading time, USV’s computation offloading, USV’s offloading time, and the secrecy provisioning. WITH the growing demands for marine activities, there has been an increasing number of marine devices deployed in the ocean [1], [2], which leads to the requirements for high-speed and low-latency marine communications [3], [4]. For instance, the marine navigation data are required for safe navigation of vessels [5]. The real-time data collection is needed for safe operation of offshore drilling platforms [6]. The underwater sensor nodes (USNs) and buoys have a large amount of hydrological data to process. The real-time voices and videos are often required for maritime rescue. To this end, the computation offloading in marine networks is of great significance to meet the growing service requirements for marine activities, and have been paid much attention by researchers in recent years.

Thanks to the advent communication and computation techniques [7], marine edge computing, which enables oceanic data processing as close to the source as possible, has been envisioned as the promising paradigm to support energy efficiency and low latency communications [8], [9]. Specifically, the marine edge computing architecture can be divided into two transmission segments, i.e., the underwater transmission segment and the radio frequency transmission segment. For the underwater segment, it covers the communication and data transmission between USNs and surface nodes, and the acoustic transmission has been regarded as an effective approach for improving the data transmission efficiency [10]. For the radio frequency segment, it provides the communication and data transmission between surface nodes and terrestrial nodes for computation offloading. However, the underwater acoustic transmission suffers from low data rate, long propagation delay, and high packet loss probability, which reduces the ondemands services in marine applications [11]. In addition, the USNs are powered by batteries, which might be quickly exhausted due to the significant consumption for overcoming the acoustic signal attenuation. Moreover, USNs are hard to be recharged due to the complicated marine environment. Therefore, it is necessary to design an energy efficient computation offloading scheme to prolong the lifetime of USNs and guarantee the reliable data transmission.

paragraph_content.content: Multi-access computation offloading in ocean environment is an effective approach to improve the computing efficiency of ocean devices [12], [13], [14]. Existing works focusing on oceanic computation offloading can be classified into two categories. One approach is to directly offload the workloads to unmanned devices (e.g., unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs)) [15]. This approach aims to save the energy consumption of USNs by path planning to shorten the data transmission distance. Another approach is to exploit the relay transmission to offload the workloads to terrestrial nodes (e.g., offshore base stations, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)) [16] for processing through multi-hop routing schemes, which requires at least one relay node between USN and terrestrial nodes [17]. This approach mainly focuses on the relay selection and routing design to improve the relay performance. Different from these offloading modes, multi-access computation offloading enables ocean devices to offload their workloads to multiple edge nodes in marine networks, which has been expected to effectively enhance the computing efficiency.

Existing works adopt the time division multiple access (TDMA) and frequency division multiple access (FDMA) for data transmission between USNs and surface nodes in the underwater environment, since there is no co-channel interference among different acoustic channels [18]. However, the TDMA requires the strict time sequence for data transmission, which results in high cost on information exchanges. The acoustic bandwidth resource utilization in FDMA is low, which degrades the transmission throughput [19]. The nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) [20], [21], which allows USNs to reuse the same resource block for data transmission, has been considered as an efficient approach to improve the channel efficiency and transmission throughput. In addition, due to the nature of radio broadcasting in radio frequency segment, malicious nodes can intentionally eavesdrop the radio signals and decode the transmission data. Therefore, the stateof-art solutions for improving the data transmission efficiency and guaranteeing secrecy provisioning in underwater environment are still the open issues.

Motivated by the above considerations, in this work, we investigate the UAV-assisted multi-access computation offloading via hybrid NOMA and FDMA in marine networks. The main contributions of this work can be summarized as follows.

We propose an energy efficient computation offloading scheme in marine networks, which consists of two transmission segments, i.e., the underwater acoustic transmission and the radio frequency transmission. In underwater acoustic transmission, multiple USNs collect sensing

data for data uploading via NOMA to improve the acoustic channel utilization. In radio frequency transmission, multiple UAVs hovering in the air provide aerial computing services as the aerial base stations, and USV offloads partial workloads to UAVs subject to the eavesdroppingattack from malicious node. We formulate a joint optimization problem of the USNs’ uploading time, USV’s computation offloading and offloading time, and the secrecy provisioning, with the objective of minimizing the total energy consumption of USNs and USV.

Despite the non-convexity of the formulated joint optimization problem, we exploit a layered structure to decompose the problem. We divide the optimization problem into a top-problem for solving the USNs’ uploading time and a sub-problem for optimizing the USV’s computation offloading and offloading time, and the secrecy provisioning. Regarding the sub-problem, given the USNs’ uploading time, USV’s offloading time and the secrecy provisioning, we first solve the optimal computation offloading for USV. Then, we propose a two-dimensional line-searching algorithm to find the optimal USV’s offloading time and the secrecy provisioning. Regarding the top-problem, we adopt the line-searching method to find the optimal USNs’ uploading time.

We finally provide simulations to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithms. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithms can obtain the minimum energy consumption, and verify the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithms in comparison with the globally optimal solution by LINGO.

The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section II provides the literature review. Section III presents the system model and problem formulation. The transformation of the joint optimization problem is presented in Section IV. Section V proposes algorithms for solving the joint optimization problem. Numerical results are shown in Section VI. Section VII closes this paper with conclusion.
This section reviews the related studies including (i) the joint computation offloading and resource allocation, and (ii) the energy efficient computation offloading in maritime networks.

Marine edge computing has been considered as a promising paradigm to improve the computation offloading efficiency in terms of energy consumption and computation latency in marine networks. There have been many studies exploiting the resource allocation for computation offloading in marine environment. In [22], Liu et al. investigated a two-layer UAVs maritime communication architecture to minimize the communication and computation latency for maritime UAV swarm mobile edge computing network. In [23], Abdel-Basset et al. proposed an energy-aware model based on the marine predators algorithm to implement the task scheduling in fog computing, with the objective of improving the quality of service (QoS) required by users. In [24], Su et al. exploited edge-based maritime networks services, in which the edge computation resource allocation is thoroughly analyzed. In [25], Liu et al. studied a spatio-temporal multi-graph convolutional network-based trajectory prediction scheme to guarantee traffic efficiency based on marine edge computing paradigm. On the other hand, fog computing has been adopted in marine communication networks, Yang et al. proposed the fog computing to Ocean of Things to reduce the amount of ocean data transmission and data processing delay [26]. In [27], a novel transmission scheduling scheme based on the enhanced deep Q-learning algorithm has been proposed in marine networks. In [28], Han et al. proposed a multi-AUV collaborative data collection algorithm based on Q-learning method to reduce the load of data collection task.

paragraph_content.content: There have been many studies investigating the energy efficient computation offloading to prolong the devices’ lifetime. In [29], a novel stochastic model has been proposed for opportunistic routing in multi-modal USNs, aiming to reduce the energy consumption and improve the network data delivery ratio. In [30], Timmins et al. studied the effect of sea surface shadowing conditions via the finite-difference time domain method on the marine communications channel. In [31], Li et al. investigated the maritime coverage enhancement using UAVs coordinated with hybrid satellite-terrestrial networks. Zeng et al. [32] established the systematic USV kinetics and information transmission models, jointly optimizing the trajectory and communication resource allocation to maximize the minimum expected throughput overall ships. In [33], a cooperative multicast communication scheme for maritime users relying on joint beamforming optimization and relay design has been proposed to increase the system throughput. In [34], an overview of a space-based network for the maritime surveillance information sharing has been provided to evaluate the coverage, throughput and real-time reception capacity of the presented systems. In [35], Yang et al. studied the green energy and content-aware data transmissions in maritime networks. Different from existing works, in this work, we exploit the energy efficient computation offloading via hybrid NOMA and FDMA in marine networks. Specifically, we consider two transmission modes, i.e., in underwater segment, these USNs upload their sensing data to USV via NOMA; in radio frequency segment, USV aggregates the collected sensing data and then partially offloads it to UAVs via FDMA. We formulate a joint optimization problem to optimize the transmission time, the offloading workloads and the secrecy provisioning, with the objective of minimizing the total energy consumption of USNs and USV.

title_content.content: III. SYSTEM MODEL AND PROBLEM FORMULATION

paragraph_content.content: This section first introduces the system model for UAVassisted multi-access computation offloading in marine networks, and the problem formulation is then proposed.

Fig. 1 illustrates the scenario of UAV-assisted multi-access computation offloading via hybrid NOMA and FDMA in marine networks, which consists of multiple USNs, one USV, multi-UAVs and an active eavesdropper. Specifically, in Phase I, the collected data from multi-USNs are uploaded to USV via NOMA. USV is responsible for collecting data from USNs through acoustic signal in underwater transmission and then transcodes data for radio frequency offloading to UAVs. In Phase II, USV receives the data from USNs through acoustic transmission and then transcodes the data for radio frequency transmission. In Phase III and Phase IV, USV processes partial workloads locally and then offloads the remained workloads to UAVs via FDMA while taking into consideration that an eavesdropper overhears the USV’s offloading transmission.

In this paper, we have investigated UAV-assisted multiaccess computation offloading via hybrid NOMA and FDMA in marine networks. In particular, two transmission segments, i.e., the underwater acoustic transmission and the radio frequency transmission, were respectively exploited for computation offloading. In underwater transmission segment, we considered multiple USNs form the NOMA cluster to upload data to USV via acoustic channels. In radio frequency transmission segment, we considered that USV offloads partial workloads to UAVs for data processing by taking into account the overhearing attack from a malicious eavesdropper in marine environment. To improve the computation offloading efficiency, we have formulated a joint optimization problem of the USN’s uploading time, USV’s computation offloading, USV’s offloading time, and the secrecy provisioning to minimize the total energy consumption of USNs and USV. We have proposed a layered structure to decompose the original problem into a top-problem and a sub-problem, in which efficient algorithms have been proposed to obtain the optimal solutions. Finally, we have conducted extensive numerical results to demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed algorithms compared with benchmark schemes. For the future work, we will investigate multi-USNs’ NOMA grouping scenario in underwater environment, in which the coalition formulation of NOMA grouping will be studied.
